text: Attempt 2 begins: attempt 1's fast start, but a fire station every ~14 tiles in every district, no airport until shops are capped (then isolated), a loan budget of ~30, taxes never cut while in debt.
Jul 2006: seaport + east dense job strip (a19-2006), homes across from it (c4-east-homes), district 5 (loans #5-6).
Jul 2007: 14 south riverbank pumps (water 0% spare), 6 fire stations from the new firegrid.py (one every ~14 tiles), stadium at (101,98) without the airport (loan #7).
Jul 2008: crossed the river (causeway y69, raised wires y68) and built the first west district (a19-west) - two years later than attempt 1 but on 9 loans instead of 16.
Jul 2010: 7 north lake pumps; airport at (84-89,114-117) on bare land 17 tiles from the nearest district, with its own fire station (loan #10).
Jul 2012: west shops band and a dense factory strip (a19-wshops, a19-wind + power joins), loan #13.
Dec 2013: pumps-mid, south districts (shops, zoo 2), power/pipe joins the new audit caught, 7 more fire stations (16 total); loans #14-16.
Dec 2014: north-west district + coal plant (38,15), joined to the grid at once (the new audit FAIL caught the attempt-1 mistake). Loan #17. 46,780 people, ahead of pace.

Dec 2014: attempt 2 is at 46,780 people - ahead of the pace line - on 17 loans (attempt 1 had 20 at a similar size and two fires behind it). 16 fire stations so far, and the airport sits alone on bare land in the south. The new audit checks already caught two mistakes that cost attempt 1 years.
Jul 2019: south-west districts 2 and 3, west-shore pumps, zoo + stadium + coal east of district 3, more fire stations (loans #18-22).
Jan 2021: two more neighbour road links (west edge y20, east edge y20 looped round a fire station) - 8% jobless while shop/factory demand was negative (loans #23-24).
Feb 2023: north-west district (c4-nw2) with its pipe and line joins, fire stations for it.
Oct 2023: river pumps by the NW district, coal plant (54,98), dense factory block in the east corner (loan #27). Small rubble near the seaport was not a fire.
Jul 2025: second rail link off the east edge beside the east factories (trade capacity); factory tax ceiling raised to 10% (demand maxed) to narrow the $8k/yr deficit. Loan #29.

Jul 2025: attempt 2 is at 87,520 people - beyond attempt 1's peak five years earlier - on 29 loans with no fires so far. Money is the next limit: the budget runs ~$8k a year short, so from here the plan is fewer loans and higher taxes where demand is maxed.
Feb 2027: 5 pumps on the fresh-water pond x94-98 y12-13 (water 9% spare). Loan #30 - the planned loan budget is now used; from here only for growth with clear payback.

Nov 2031: growth stalled at ~95,600 with all demand negative; cash -$28k falling ~$7.6k/yr would hit the -$100k game-over around 2040. Taxes raised to homes 11 / shops 10 / factories 10, controller floor 10%.
Nov 2033: the tax rise backfired - 95,600 -> 80,850 people, 22% jobless, income fell with them. Taxes back to 8/7/8.

Sep-Oct 2036: a monster wrecked the coal plants by the seaport. With cash at -$71k nothing can be rebuilt; attempt 2 peaked at 95,620 (Nov 2031) and is running out its debt. The big lesson for attempt 3 is money: 30 loans cost $15k a year and the city never earned enough to carry them - growth stalled near 95,000 with all demand negative.
Jun 2038: cash -$93k; factory demand at the 2,000 maximum, so factory tax to 14% and homes to 9% to try to stay above the -$100k game-over at the January budget.
Nov 2038: the game crashed to DOS while the tax controller worked the budget window (not a disaster); reloaded the Nov 2038 save C4A2.SC2 and carried on.
